classification.difficultyReason: Development: beyond reading two individual columns, the hardest part requires comparing aggregate weekly sales and explaining why coffee's combined daily excess outweighs tea's Thursday excess. This routinely links the taught scale-reading and contextual comparison methods.

content.prompt: The column graph shows sales of tea and coffee on five different days at a café.

spec.description: Five weekday pairs, tea on the left and coffee on the right, with a boxed key outside the plotting area. Both axes have arrows. Frequency ticks run from 0 to 50 in tens. Fine graph-paper lines are retained provisionally. There is no graph title or horizontal-axis title.
spec.mathematics: Approximate reconstruction coordinates, not additional exact student givens: Monday tea about 26 and coffee about 38; Tuesday tea about 12 and coffee 45; Wednesday tea about 26 and coffee about 31; Thursday tea about 43 and coffee about 40; Friday tea approximately 20 and coffee about 47. The Friday tea coordinate 19.8 preserves the source's slightly below-line appearance and does not assert decimal data. No bar-value labels are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is permanently visible. Answers and weekly totals are not included.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many teas were sold on Friday?

answer.worked: The Friday tea column reaches approximately $20$ on the frequency scale, so approximately $20$ teas were sold.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many coffees were sold on Tuesday?

answer.worked: The Tuesday coffee column is halfway between $40$ and $50$, so $45$ coffees were sold.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Did the café sell more teas or coffees over the week? Explain how you know.

answer.short: More coffees. Coffee’s combined excess on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday exceeds tea’s smaller Thursday excess.
answer.worked: Coffee sales exceed tea sales on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Together, these differences are greater than the small excess of tea sales on Thursday. Therefore, more coffees were sold over the week.
